kind: multi_country_interest

buttonLabel: "Wildlife on the route through Bolivia and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  The 32-day tour through Bolivia and Uruguay includes wildlife encounters in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. Bolivia's lagoons offer opportunities to see flamingos during a scenic 4×4 expedition, while the Uruguayan section focuses on Montevideo. We compare this itinerary with a 20-day nature journey and explain which experiences take place in which countries.
---

## Where can you see wildlife on tours including Bolivia and Uruguay?

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Bolivia and Uruguay as main countries and the “Wildlife and Safaris” theme assigned to the route. It features the 32-day tour with a Galápagos section. The 20-day tour discussed below is included for comparison: it has the “Nature” theme but not “Wildlife and Safaris”. This **does not mean that nature excursions are included in both selected countries**. On the [20-day journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day journey through eight](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), the Uruguayan section is devoted to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). The main nature-focused days within the selected pair take place in Bolivia.

What matters is the actual daily programme, not the number of countries or a thematic label. Uruguay's excursion introduces the port, old town and Independence Square. The itinerary **does not specify a visit to a nature reserve, a marine safari or whale watching** on that day. Even if such experiences are available elsewhere in the country, they are not automatically part of the paid tour.

## Laguna Colorada: flamingos at high altitude

The road into Bolivia comes after Chile's Atacama. In 4×4 vehicles, travellers cross high-altitude landscapes towards [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Its reddish waters, mineral-rich shores and flamingos make it one of the Altiplano's recognisable natural sites.

Birds may be observed in their natural feeding grounds, but their behaviour and distance from visitors change. Visiting the lagoon does not guarantee a particular number or species of flamingos, or a good close-range photograph. Responsible wildlife watching means keeping your distance rather than approaching the birds for a picture.

The next travel day includes the Honda, Hedionda, Chiar Khota and Cañapa lagoons. Conditions differ between them: depth, salinity, shoreline and the availability of water affect each habitat. Encounters can therefore vary even when several lakes are visited in succession.

Bolivia's protected-area system recognises the high-altitude lagoons and the Eduardo Avaroa reserve as important for Andean fauna. This is a reason to travel with care, not a guarantee of rare-animal sightings.

## The Uyuni Salt Flats: a landscape, not a safari

After the high-altitude lagoons, the itineraries lead to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The salt flat is remarkable for its vast open space, salt surface and reflections during rainy periods. But Uyuni itself is primarily **a landscape stop**. Do not assume the same concentration of waterbirds as at the Altiplano's lakes.

If birds are the main goal, allow sufficient time at the lagoons. If photography of the salt plain matters more, stops need to be prioritised differently. Discuss this before booking: a standard two-day overland itinerary includes roads, geothermal areas, lagoons and the salt flat itself.

For more options, explore [nature tours in Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/) and the individual [Laguna Colorada page](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). These help distinguish actual birdwatching from a general scenic excursion.

## What will travellers experience in Uruguay?

Both programmes include a ferry journey from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, with a city tour and return on the same day. This section focuses on architecture and urban life beside the Río de la Plata. No specialist excursion to Uruguay's natural areas is included.

That limitation matters when comparing alternatives. If a traveller wants to watch birds specifically in Uruguay, a new nature-focused programme and additional time must be discussed separately. A potentially available excursion cannot be presented as already included.

“Wildlife and Safaris” is assigned to the 32-day journey because its Galápagos section in Ecuador includes opportunities for animal observation. The 20-day tour does not carry that theme. Both also visit nature sites **in other countries**, including Iguazú Falls in Argentina and Brazil, but waterfalls alone do not make a tour a safari. The Galápagos experiences must not be geographically attributed to Uruguay or Bolivia.

## Comparing the current itineraries

| Question | What the programmes include |
|---|---|
| Uyuni and Altiplano lagoons | Both tours |
| Visit to Montevideo | Both tours |
| Galápagos nature section | Only the 32-day tour |
| Shorter of the two options | 20 days, 6 countries |

The table below compares programmes with wildlife or birdwatching experiences. Scenic journeys without such activities can be compared under [nature travel](/multi-country/bolivia_uruguay/interests/nature/). On a multi-country tour, wildlife observation may take place outside the countries named in the category title: check the complete route and specific days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [20-day route](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) suits those wanting Bolivia, Uruguay and other key South American stops without the longer continuation. The [32-day route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) adds separate stages in Ecuador and Colombia, including a dedicated introduction to Galápagos wildlife.

Compare programmes by the actual number of nature days, guide languages, logistics, demands of transfers and specific included excursions. All journeys involving the selected two countries appear in the [Bolivia + Uruguay catalogue](/multi-country/bolivia_uruguay/), while other multi-country wildlife journeys feature under [“Wildlife and Safaris”](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/).

## High mountains and an urban waterfront: viewing conditions

Bolivia's lagoons lie at high altitude. Cold mornings, wind, strong sunshine and thin air affect comfort and the duration of stops. Warm windproof clothing, sunglasses and suitable footwear are important. Binoculars or a camera with a telephoto lens help observe birds from a respectful distance; provision of this equipment is not confirmed in the programmes.

Montevideo calls for entirely different preparation: everyday city clothing and enough time for the ferry. Because the tours cross Argentina, Chile and other countries, weather, entry requirements and payment arrangements must be reviewed for each stage. For Russian citizens and travellers of other nationalities, checks are based on the actual passport, including any re-entry to Argentina after Uruguay.

Ada Tours helps coordinate a realistic pace and match the route to each traveller's nature interests. Weather and animal encounters, however, remain outside the organiser's control.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia and Uruguay

### Will there be wildlife watching in both countries?

There is no dedicated wildlife programme in both countries. In Bolivia, birds may be seen during a scenic 4×4 expedition; in Uruguay, a sightseeing tour of Montevideo is scheduled. The included Galápagos wildlife stage is only on the 32-day itinerary and takes place in Ecuador.

### Where should I look for flamingos?

Primarily around [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and nearby high-altitude lakes. Sightings depend on natural conditions and cannot be guaranteed.

### Is visiting Uyuni necessary for wildlife?

Uyuni is chiefly a salt flat and a salt-landscape attraction. The Altiplano lagoons, included in the same off-road section, are more important for birdwatching.

### Are the Galápagos included in both journeys?

No. The Galápagos Islands form a separate Ecuadorian stage of the 32-day programme. This additional nature experience does not take place in Bolivia or Uruguay.

targetPath: /multi-country/bolivia_venezuela/
kind: multi_country_combination
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore tours in Bolivia and Venezuela"
lead: >-
  Bolivia and Venezuela connect two very different natural worlds in South America: Caribbean islands and waterfalls among Venezuela's tepuis, and the high-altitude Uyuni Salt Flats and colourful Andean lagoons in Bolivia. Ada Tours lists a 12-day itinerary through Caracas, Los Roques, Canaima, La Paz and Uyuni. Before choosing it, pay particular attention to safety in Venezuela, flight availability, border documents, insurance and the sudden change from the tropics to elevations above 3,500 metres.
---

## Bolivia and Venezuela: connecting the Caribbean and the Andes

**Bolivia and Venezuela do not share a land border.** Travelling between them involves air connections, subject to available routes and possible transfers. Their appeal lies chiefly in their contrasts: Venezuela offers the Caribbean Sea, rainforest, rivers and table-top mountains; Bolivia offers high-altitude cities, salt flats, lagoons and volcanic landscapes.

The Venezuelan section of Ada Tours' programme includes [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), the [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) islands and [Canaima with Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). Bolivia includes [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), high-altitude lagoons and the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/).

These stops involve different demands and require entirely different preparation. At Los Roques, the principal activities revolve around the sea and hot weather. In Canaima, motorboat rides and a walk to a viewpoint are included. In Bolivia, travellers quickly move to elevations where oxygen is scarce, nights can be cold and emergency medical care in remote areas is limited.

For background on each country, explore the [Venezuela](/venezuela/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) guides. Here the question is more specific: how to assess **whether a journey combining both countries is realistically feasible and safe**.

## Which two-country journeys does Ada Tours offer?

This catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Bolivia and Venezuela in the main itinerary. The confirmed option is [“Nature and Culture of Venezuela and Bolivia in 12 Days”](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). It is a single programme, starting in Venezuela, continuing in Bolivia and returning via Caracas.

| Stage | Included destinations |
|---|---|
| Venezuela, days 1–7 | Caracas, Los Roques, Canaima, Angel Falls |
| Bolivia, days 8–11 | La Paz, Uyuni, Incahuasi, lagoons and geysers |
| Day 12 | Return via La Paz and Caracas |

The first days include an introduction to Caracas, a flight to Los Roques and time on the islands. The programme then moves to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/): a boat journey across the lagoon, El Sapo and Hacha Falls, followed the next day by a motorboat trip up the Carrao River towards Salto Ángel and a walk to the viewpoint. Another day is reserved for relaxing by the lagoon. Additional flights and active excursions mentioned as options must not be assumed to be included in the base price.

Day eight specifies a flight from Caracas to La Paz. This is followed by a city tour, a flight to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Incahuasi Island with its giant cacti, the Train Cemetery, desert rock formations and lagoons. The high-altitude section features Laguna Colorada, [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), hot springs, the Salvador Dalí Desert and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) beneath Licancabur.

**The 12-day schedule is the structure of the published itinerary, not confirmation that every flight will operate on any chosen date.** The international connection and final day require particular attention, as the programme specifies a return from Bolivia to Caracas followed by another international departure. Actual connections, durations and feasibility need to be agreed separately.

## Safety in Venezuela: the main question before booking

**As of 15 October 2026, travel to Venezuela requires particular caution and a separate assessment of whether the itinerary is advisable.** The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) updated its advice on 14 October: it advised against all travel to certain parts of Venezuela and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country, including major urban destinations. These are UK government risk assessments; travellers of other nationalities should check the advice issued by their own countries as well.

Official information mentions safety concerns, limited availability of certain services and **restricted international air connections**. Although the airport serving Caracas resumed commercial operations on 1 September 2026, capacity remained limited. A temporarily unavailable flight, a route change or a cancelled connection could disrupt the whole two-country journey, not just one day.

Bolivia, meanwhile, must not automatically be treated as subject to identical warnings throughout the country. The FCDO identifies specific Bolivian regions, including Chapare, and notes risks from protests, roadblocks and transport disruption. The La Paz and Uyuni itinerary should be assessed on its own conditions and the current situation, rather than extending warnings to every Bolivian region.

Before booking, practical questions must be answered: do safety advisories and insurance terms permit visiting the particular areas? Are the planned flights operating? Is there a realistic contingency plan if transport is cancelled? Can travellers be evacuated from a remote natural area? **Insurance may exclude trips to places a government authority advises people not to visit.** An available tourism product does not remove these risks.

If safety and adequate insurance coverage cannot be confirmed, **postponing the journey or selecting another region** is more sensible. The decision must be based on actual circumstances, not only on the attractiveness of the sights.

## Flights and the transition from lowlands to highlands

Distances on a map can be deceptive. Venezuela's islands, Canaima and Caracas already require domestic flights and water transfers. The route then moves to Bolivia, where further flights and lengthy overland journeys at altitude follow.

Do not promise a nonstop Caracas–La Paz flight or a particular journey time in advance: a published tour is not an airline timetable. Before confirming the itinerary, compare available air routes, possible transit countries, airport changes, baggage allowances and documents required at each connection. When flights are limited, an extra contingency day may be more valuable than another excursion.

**The sudden gain in altitude** demands special attention. After Caribbean islands and tropical Canaima, travellers arrive in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), where many parts of the city are well above 3,500 metres. The route then continues to the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and even higher: the published itinerary includes an overnight stay at approximately 4,400 metres and a visit to the Sol de Mañana geothermal area at nearly 5,000 metres.

Altitude sickness is possible at these elevations, and fitness does not guarantee immunity. Discuss the route and an acceptable pace of ascent with a doctor beforehand, especially if you have cardiovascular or respiratory conditions. On the journey, it is important to monitor symptoms, allow appropriate acclimatisation and be prepared to change the programme if someone becomes unwell. Emergency medical care is harder to access in remote mountain areas.

## Documents, vaccinations and health insurance

Bolivia and Venezuela have **separate entry requirements**. Visas, permitted entries, passport validity, children's documents and transit arrangements depend on nationality and the exact itinerary. FCDO advice for British passport holders must not be applied mechanically to Russian or other passports.

Repeat entry is especially important on this itinerary: Bolivia follows the Venezuelan section, then the programme returns via Caracas. Checking permission for the first arrival in Venezuela is therefore insufficient. Confirm whether the travel authorisation allows re-entry and whether all segments pass through official immigration checkpoints.

Another important consideration is **yellow fever**. Official UK guidance for Bolivia describes a requirement for a vaccination certificate when arriving from a country categorised as a risk area. This needs particular checking for the Venezuela → Bolivia sequence, taking account of current health classifications, places visited, age and contraindications. Other advice on infection prevention and protection against mosquitoes varies by region.

Seek medical advice before purchasing non-refundable tickets. Review not just whether an insurance policy exists but what it actually covers:
- Canaima, river journeys and remote natural areas;
- the elevations of the specific Bolivian stages and planned activities;
- emergency hospital treatment and medical evacuation;
- flight cancellations and restrictions linked to official safety advisories.

Vaccination and prevention decisions belong with a doctor, and the insurer should confirm that coverage applies to the actual programme. The name of a travel insurance policy is not enough to prove protection.

## Money: bolivianos, bolívares and a reserve for difficult stages

Bolivia uses the **boliviano (BOB)** and Venezuela the **bolívar (VES)**. US dollars may be used for some payments and currency exchange, but rates, access to cash and acceptance of foreign bank cards vary by location and circumstances. On a journey with many flights, it is advisable to organise personal spending money by country.

In Venezuela especially, payment arrangements and financial infrastructure can be unpredictable. Official UK guidance notes that some merchants accept US dollars and international cards, but terminals may not work with particular foreign-issued cards. Relying on a single payment card is risky.

Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks generally cannot be used for international transactions in these countries. For a foreign-issued card, check the issuer, network, geographical restrictions, cash withdrawals and fees. Do not assume that currency exchange will be equally accessible in Caracas, Los Roques and remote camps.

Check separately which transfers, domestic flights, admission tickets, meals and excursions **are actually included in the chosen tour**. The 12-day programme lists domestic flights within Venezuela and Bolivia, but that does not establish that every international segment or intercontinental ticket is paid for. The price cannot be inferred from the duration or hotel list.

## When to travel and what to pack

There is no single ideal season for the whole Venezuela–Bolivia trip. In Canaima, river levels affect the character of boat journeys and the waterfalls. At Los Roques, wind and sea conditions matter. Around Uyuni in Bolivia, rains may create a reflective surface on the salt flat while making some areas inaccessible. In the dry season, road travel is often easier, but nights in the highlands can be very cold.

Pack for two contrasting climates. For the Caribbean and tropics, bring light clothing, protection against sun, rain and insects, and shoes for wet paths. For [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), bring warm layers, wind protection, closed shoes, sunglasses and protection from intense high-altitude sunlight.

Check the weight and dimensions allowed on all domestic flights beforehand. On difficult water and overland sections, a small daypack for documents, water, essentials and waterproof protection for electronics is useful.

## Frequently asked questions about a Bolivia + Venezuela tour

### Does Ada Tours offer an existing itinerary covering both countries?

Yes. We offer the [12-day Venezuela and Bolivia tour](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) through Caracas, Los Roques, Canaima, La Paz and Uyuni. Whether it can operate on specific dates depends on actual flights, safety and travel conditions.

### Could Venezuela be considered safe for tourists in October 2026?

That conclusion cannot be made. **On 14 October 2026, the FCDO updated serious warnings**, advising against all travel to some areas and all but essential travel to others. Check your own country's advice, insurance and conditions at every stop. If the trip cannot be organised safely, it should be postponed.

### Must the flight between Caracas and La Paz be nonstop?

No nonstop service is required. What matters is having a viable routing with permitted transit arrangements and a realistic duration. The itinerary involves travel from Caracas to La Paz, but the actual flights must be confirmed before booking.

### Are 12 days enough for the tropics and highlands?

The published journey lasts 12 days, but it is intensive: domestic flights, boat trips and ascent to nearly 5,000 metres. Feasibility depends on flights, travellers' health and adequate acclimatisation. Adding days or simplifying the itinerary may be wiser.

### Which matters more: a visa or medical documents?

Both. Alongside visas and re-entry conditions, the Venezuela → Bolivia sequence requires a separate check of yellow-fever certificate and health-insurance requirements. The details depend on nationality, places visited and current regulations.

### Can Los Roques beaches and Uyuni be combined?

Yes. That is the central idea of the [existing itinerary](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). But the transition from tropical weather to the highlands calls for suitable clothing, health assessment and careful planning of altitude gain.

### What needs checking before paying?

First, whether the journey is advisable under safety guidance and insurance terms, confirmed flights, entry and re-entry arrangements, medical requirements, paid flight inclusions, accommodation and options to adjust the route after a cancellation. Only then should dates and the itinerary be finalised.

Ada Tours can help compare [Bolivian routes](/bolivia/tour/) with [Venezuela journeys](/venezuela/tour/), discuss combining the countries and design a custom trip within services that are genuinely available and can be organised safely. Given existing restrictions, a different country sequence or postponement may be the more sensible choice.

## Beach holidays on a Venezuela–Bolivia tour: Los Roques and the Andean highlands

Our [Venezuela–Bolivia beach-themed selection](/multi-country/bolivia_venezuela/interests/beach-holidays/) features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The product is the [12-day “Nature and Culture of Venezuela and Bolivia” tour](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). Its beach section takes place **only in Venezuela**, in the [Los Roques archipelago](/venezuela/place/los-roques/). The Bolivian stage focuses on mountains, cities and the Uyuni Salt Flats; it has no seaside resorts.

This format suits travellers wishing to combine a few days on the Caribbean with Angel Falls and Bolivia's natural areas. If your main aim is to spend the entire holiday on a beach, choose a different balance of days or a separate route from the [beach holidays catalogue](/interests/beach-holidays/).

## Los Roques: how much seaside time is included?

After arriving in Caracas, travellers take a domestic flight to Los Roques. On day two, the programme includes relaxation on Madrisquí or Francisquí Island: light sand, clear water and time by the sea. A sun lounger, packed lunch with drinks and dinner are provided that day.

Beach time continues on day three, but **the flight back to Caracas is already scheduled for the afternoon**. Breakfast and a packed lunch are included. When planning, remember that these are not three full beach days: day one involves arrival, day two is devoted to the archipelago, and day three includes the return to the mainland.

Optional visits to distant islands, a sea turtle conservation site or natural pools, as well as fishing, are listed as possible add-ons. They are not automatically included in the price and need to be agreed separately. Weather and sea conditions also affect small boat operations and which island can be visited.

## After the beaches: Canaima and Angel Falls

On day four, travellers fly to Canaima. The programme includes a boat ride on the lagoon, Anatoly Island and a visit to Sapo Falls. The next day is devoted to motorboat travel along the Carrao River and a walk to an Angel Falls viewpoint. Another day is reserved for relaxation by the lagoon and optional activities by agreement.

This is a very different experience from Los Roques. River trips and walks require suitable footwear, clothes for humid tropical conditions, a raincoat and waterproof protection for belongings. The nature excursion includes a walk through forest, with the sequence depending on local conditions. Helicopter flights and other activities are available separately and are not part of the basic excursion.

## Bolivia: La Paz, Uyuni and high-altitude lagoons

After Venezuela, the itinerary moves to Bolivia. In La Paz, travellers discover the city, squares, cable car and Valley of the Moon. They then continue to the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Incahuasi Island and smaller lagoons in the southwest. The stops include the Train Cemetery, Valley of Rocks, the Sol de Mañana geysers, Polques hot springs and Laguna Verde.

**Bolivia is a high-altitude nature expedition on this route, not an extension of the beach holiday.** One overnight stay is at approximately 4,400 metres, with some sections higher still. After the warm Caribbean, travellers need clothing for cold nights, wind and intense Andean sunlight. Rapid altitude gain makes it especially important to discuss acclimatisation and individual health limitations in advance.

| Journey section | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Los Roques, Venezuela | White beaches and Caribbean Sea |
| Canaima, Venezuela | Lagoons, boats and Angel Falls |
| La Paz and Uyuni, Bolivia | Highlands, lagoons and salt flats |

## Planning for a combination of beaches and mountains

The biggest difference is in travel conditions. At Los Roques, bring light beach luggage, sun protection and comfortable footwear for sand and boats. In Canaima, you will need waterproof layers and shoes suitable for wet trails. In Bolivia, warm clothing and wind protection are essential. Plan to bring cold-weather gear from the outset rather than relying on buying it en route on the day of a high-altitude excursion.

The journey also involves several domestic flights and different forms of baggage transport. Before booking, check weight restrictions on local flights, connections and the actual time available by the sea. Entry and transit arrangements depend on nationality and must be checked separately for Venezuela and Bolivia.

We help agree the itinerary, transport and preferred balance between relaxation and excursions. If two days on the islands feel too short, an individually extended beach section can be discussed. This is **a separate change to the tour**, not a service already included. Other journeys involving two or more countries appear in the [multi-country catalogue](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Venezuela–Bolivia beach journey

### Are there beaches on the Bolivian stage?

No. The tour's seaside relaxation takes place at Los Roques in Venezuela. The Bolivian days focus on La Paz, Uyuni and high-altitude natural sites.

### How much time is available on the Caribbean?

The principal beach time is on day two and the first part of day three. The flight back to Caracas is scheduled for the afternoon of day three. A longer stay on the islands would require a programme change.

### Can diving be added to this itinerary?

The basic beach programme includes seaside relaxation and possible optional island visits, but a dedicated diving programme is not confirmed. It must be arranged separately, subject to available operators and free time.

### How different are the climates?

Very different. The Caribbean archipelago, humid Canaima and cold Bolivian highlands require different clothing. Bolivia also presents challenges associated with altitude.

lead: >-
  On a 12-day journey through Venezuela and Bolivia, cultural experiences change with the geography: sightseeing in Caracas, the Santa Teresa estate and an introduction to Pemón traditions in Canaima are followed by La Paz, its Witches' Market, Plaza Murillo and cable car. Caribbean islands and high-altitude salt flats lie between these experiences. This is one journey offering different introductions to local life, not two separate city sightseeing tours.
---

## The cultures of Venezuela and Bolivia on one itinerary

[Venezuela](/venezuela/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/) rarely feel alike to travellers. The former offers the Caribbean Sea, Canaima's humid forests and lively Caracas. The latter reveals a high-altitude capital, city markets, everyday Andean life and settlements around the Uyuni Salt Flats. For travellers interested in people, crafts and historical connections, these changes matter as much as the landscapes.

Our thematic catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Its principal product is the [12-day “Nature and Culture of Venezuela and Bolivia” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). Consider the whole programme: the first half takes place in Venezuela, followed by a flight to La Paz and final days on Bolivia's Altiplano. There is no direct overland sightseeing transfer between the capitals.

| Country | Cultural experiences |
|---|---|
| Venezuela | Caracas, Santa Teresa estate, Pemón traditions |
| Bolivia | La Paz, Witches' Market, Plaza Murillo, rural settlements |

## Caracas and the history of the Santa Teresa estate

The introduction to Venezuela begins in [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/). A sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide is scheduled after resting on the day of arrival. The city stands among mountain slopes, and its panorama illustrates how urban development occupies different elevations.

On day seven, the group returns to Caracas and travels to the valley containing the Santa Teresa estate. Sugar cane is grown here and rum is produced. The excursion visits plantations, historic buildings, the house museum and the Criadero de Solera cellar before introducing the modern production area and including a tasting. This is one of the itinerary's richest stops for cultural and industrial heritage. Lunch that day is paid for separately.

An important distinction: visiting the estate explores the history of production and a Creole family, not a generic tasting programme covering South America's wineries. The tour determines the exact visits and tasting arrangements.

## Canaima: meeting the Pemón people in a natural setting

[Canaima National Park and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) occupy a central place on the Venezuelan journey. UNESCO highlights the tepuis, sheer cliffs and waterfalls as remarkable features of the area. The programme includes a trip on a local curiara canoe around the lagoon, a walk behind El Sapo Falls and a separate excursion visit to a Pemón village.

The village visit connects a nature day with the human side of travel. Canaima is home to local communities, so their customs and way of life deserve attention in their own right. However, the programme **does not promise a multi-day ethnographic stay or participation in rituals**. Activities such as tepui trekking, kayaking and sightseeing flights are presented as optional alternatives.

The main excursion to Salto Ángel involves a motorboat, travel through forest and a walk to a viewpoint. Cultural experiences and the demands of nature excursions should be considered together, since days in Canaima depend on river levels and local transport arrangements.

## La Paz: a high-altitude city and its traditions

In Bolivia, the journey continues in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). After arrival, a visit to the Killi Killi viewpoint, a cable-car ride and a walk through central streets are scheduled. Named stops include Plaza Murillo, government buildings, San Francisco Cathedral and the Witches' Market. The day ends at the Valley of the Moon with its geological formations.

Travellers are drawn to the Witches' Market by its local trading culture and the way traditional beliefs coexist with life in a major city. Visiting with a guide is preferable: a guide can explain the use of different items, distinguish everyday souvenirs from ritual goods and help visitors interact respectfully with vendors. The cable car offers a different perspective on the city and its neighbourhoods.

After La Paz comes the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). In Colchani, travellers can visit a settlement associated with salt production, then continue towards the “eyes of the salt flat” and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) with its giant cacti. These are primarily natural sites; the excursion does not automatically become an ethnographic journey through several communities.

## A cultural journey or a nature holiday?

The “Culture and History” and [“Nature”](/interests/nature/) themes come together on this itinerary. Cultural visits alternate with days when the landscape takes centre stage. Excursions to waterfalls, salt flats and lagoons do not amount to a separate safari or scheduled wildlife-watching programme.

In Venezuela, the main nature stops are the beaches of [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) and Angel Falls. In Bolivia, they are the salt flats, lagoons, Sol de Mañana geysers and Laguna Verde. Travellers wanting to spend most of the trip in museums, archaeological complexes and cities should check how much time is devoted to nature. For instance, the famous Tiwanaku archaeological complex is **not included on this 12-day route**, even though it is in Bolivia and attracts history enthusiasts.

For more cultural options, compare [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and [Latin American culture and history programmes](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Logistics, flights and expenses

After the islands and Canaima, the group returns to Caracas; day eight involves an international flight from Caracas to La Paz. Domestic flights in Venezuela and Bolivia are listed among included services, while the **Caracas–La Paz–Caracas** flights and intercontinental tickets are specified separately. Since these are different flight categories, the total price of the two-country tour cannot be compared without examining which tickets are included.

The Venezuelan bolívar and Bolivian boliviano are different currencies. Payments and cash require a separate plan for each country, taking account of the actual traveller's payment options. We help coordinate the sequence of transfers, expenses and questions to settle before departure. Acceptance of any specific foreign or Russian bank card at a particular shop cannot be promised.

Entry, transit, passport validity and document requirements must be checked separately for each nationality. For Venezuela, review current official safety advisories, domestic flight routes and insurance coverage. These questions depend on travel dates, not the generic label “two South American countries”.

## What to pack for the transition from the Caribbean to the Altiplano

On Venezuela's islands, clothing for hot weather and sun protection are needed; in Canaima, footwear for wet trails, a raincoat and dry clothes after boat travel. Bolivia takes the journey to entirely different elevations. The programme includes an overnight stay around 4,400 metres and an ascent to the geysers at nearly 5,000 metres; cold and strong wind are possible even in sunshine.

Flying from lowland Venezuela to high-altitude La Paz changes conditions abruptly. Ordinary physical fitness does not predict altitude tolerance: preparation should include discussing gradual acclimatisation and health with a doctor familiar with high-altitude travel. If a more relaxed pace is required, the sequence and permissible changes to days should be agreed in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about the cultures of Venezuela and Bolivia

### Does the tour introduce travellers to local traditions?

Yes. A Pemón village visit is included in Canaima, and La Paz features a walk through the centre and Witches' Market. These offer different forms of cultural experience, not an extended specialist ethnographic expedition.

### Is the Tiwanaku archaeological complex included?

No. The Bolivian section visits La Paz, Uyuni and natural areas of the southwest. Tiwanaku is not listed on the selected 12-day programme.

### How do travellers move between Venezuela and Bolivia?

The itinerary specifies air travel between Caracas and La Paz. In the current list of exclusions, Caracas–La Paz–Caracas tickets are charged separately. Exact connections and entry requirements must be confirmed for the selected dates.

### Is the trip suitable for someone without high-altitude experience?

Suitability must be assessed individually. After lowland Venezuela, the route reaches La Paz and parts of Bolivia above 4,000 metres; acclimatisation time, suitable clothing and medical risk assessment are essential.

## Nature in Venezuela and Bolivia: from the Caribbean to the Altiplano

At first glance, Venezuela and Bolivia appear to be two entirely different holidays. In Venezuela, travellers encounter turquoise Caribbean water, white-sand islands and towering tepui rock walls from which waterfalls plunge. Bolivia reveals dry high-altitude plains, the Uyuni Salt Flats, lagoons and geothermal fields. Ada Tours combines these natural contrasts into one 12-day itinerary.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: [“Nature and Culture of Venezuela and Bolivia in 12 Days”](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). Besides the natural attractions, the tour features Caracas, encounters with local culture and transfers between regions. It is worth understanding how its two geographical sections are arranged.

## Venezuela: islands, lagoons and Angel Falls

### Los Roques: relaxing beside the Caribbean

After arriving in Caracas, travellers fly to the [Los Roques archipelago](/venezuela/place/los-roques/). Here the water is strikingly clear, with many shades of blue. Shallow seas and sandy shores surround the small islands. On Madrisquí or Francisquí Island, the programme includes relaxation, sun loungers and a packed lunch with drinks. The following day brings more beach time and the return to Caracas.

An important distinction: trips to more distant islands, sea turtle viewing sites and sea fishing are listed as optional extras. They should not be counted as part of the standard package unless specifically agreed.

### Canaima: table-top mountains and waterfalls

The next major nature section is [Canaima National Park and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). This is the land of tepuis: mountains with nearly vertical rock faces and flat tops. UNESCO highlights their unusual geology and the extraordinary height of Canaima's waterfalls.

The itinerary separately lists Canaima Lagoon, Sapo and Hacha Falls, a journey to Salto Ángel and a visit to a Pemón community. Waterfalls in this part of Venezuela are affected by seasonal river levels, so viewing conditions and access to individual routes should be checked for the travel dates. A flight, river journey and walk to a viewpoint are not interchangeable: the inclusions for each day are specified on the tour page.

## Bolivia: salt, cacti and high-altitude lagoons

### La Paz and the change in elevation

On day eight, the itinerary moves to its Bolivian section in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). Conditions change dramatically compared with the Caribbean coast: higher elevation, drier air and different temperatures. Even on a sightseeing visit, a moderate pace after the flight is advisable.

From La Paz, travellers continue towards [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The white salt plain is remarkable for its unusual sense of distance: the level expanse offers few familiar landmarks. Reflections may appear in places after rainfall, but a mirror effect cannot be promised for a specific date.

### Incahuasi, colourful lagoons and geysers

The standard route includes [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) and its giant cacti. The itinerary then crosses smaller lagoons and rocky valleys. On day eleven, it lists the Stone Tree, hot springs, [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/).

This is nature very different from Venezuela: open skies, volcanic slopes, salt and lakes whose hues vary with light and minerals. The Bolivian programme includes driving across remote areas. Warm clothing and protection from wind and sun are important even if you are not planning to trek.

| 1 | Caracas | Arrival and introduction to the city |

This sequence follows the current [12-day tour](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). It helps you assess time for rest: some days are taken up by flights, meetings and transfers, and longer nature experiences are concentrated in particular stages.

## What to plan before travelling

The most significant consideration is the change in environments. One trip calls for items suited to humid heat, the beach and remote high-altitude regions. Air travel is needed between Venezuela and Bolivia. In the source programme, international flights and some other air segments are listed as exclusions, so assess the price together with “Included” and “Not Included”, rather than just the first amount shown.

Weather is especially important for Canaima and travel across the Uyuni Salt Flats. In the rainy season, the waterfalls may be fuller, but some water and overland routes become more difficult. At Uyuni, rain increases the chance of reflections while restricting certain crossings. Excursion sequences should be matched to seasonal conditions.

Bolivia's section is at high altitude. Ascent from lowland regions can cause unpleasant symptoms even among fit travellers. Those with medical contraindications should discuss the route with a doctor beforehand; if altitude-sickness symptoms appear, do not force further ascent. Entry requirements for Venezuela, Bolivia and transit airports depend on nationality and current rules, to be checked for the specific journey.

## Who this journey suits

This itinerary suits travellers who want to combine memorable natural landscapes, are comfortable with flights and prefer organised excursions to a long independent expedition. For travellers focused mainly on Angel Falls, time in Canaima and the season are the priorities; for those drawn to open high-altitude landscapes, it is the Bolivian stages and the opportunity to see Uyuni.

Explore [all nature journeys](/interests/nature/) or [multi-country nature itineraries](/multi-country/interests/nature/). If you want a different balance of days between Los Roques, Canaima and the Altiplano, mention this when contacting Ada Tours.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can Angel Falls and Uyuni both be seen in 12 days?

Yes. Both are included in the current 12-day Venezuela–Bolivia itinerary, alongside Los Roques and other stops.

### Is Los Roques purely a beach holiday?

On this programme, most of the island stay is devoted to relaxation. Separate marine activities are offered as optional extras, so they should be agreed in advance.

### When does Uyuni have a mirror-like surface?

Reflections occur when water is present on the salt flat, more often during the rainy season. Neither reflections nor access to a particular part can be guaranteed for a particular date.

### Is it difficult to go straight from the Caribbean to the Altiplano?

Adaptation to altitude and protection against sun and cold are necessary. Even without active trekking, long transfers and a change in climate can be tiring. Discuss the pace and any restrictions before booking.
